Sura 49 (al-Hujurat), Madaniyya (Medinan). It has 1,475 letters, 343 words, and 18 verses.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Abdawi narrated to us, reading it to him in the year 384 AH. He said: Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Adl narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym al-Mada'ini narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites al-Hujurat will be given ten good deeds for each person who obeyed Allah and each person who disobeyed Him." [60] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/214.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger.﴾ The majority of reciters read ﴿tuqaddimu﴾ with a dammah on the ta' and a kasrah on the dal, from taqdim (putting forward). Al-Dahhak and Ya'qub read it with a fathah on both, from taqaddum (going forward). The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Do not speak contrary to the Book and the Sunnah."

Atiyya narrated from him: "Do not speak before his speech."

Abd Allah ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Umar ibn al-Hasan ibn Malik al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id ibn Uthman al-Khazzaz narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn Mahariq Abu Janada narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Salama, from al-Sab'i, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, concerning ﴿do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾, that it refers to the slaughtering on the day of al-Adha (Eid al-Adha). Al-Hasan held this view and said: "Do not slaughter before the Prophet (ﷺ) slaughters. Some Muslims slaughtered before the Prophet's (ﷺ) prayer, so he ordered them to repeat the slaughter."

Abd al-Khaliq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Hayy narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Awwam al-Riyahi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: al-Nu'man ibn Abd al-Salam al-Taymi narrated to us, from Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl, from Yahya ibn Abd Allah al-Taymi, from Habbal ibn Rufayda, from Masruq, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), concerning His saying ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾, she said: "Do not fast before your Prophet fasts."

It was also narrated from Masruq: "I entered upon Aisha on the day I came [to her], and she said to the slave-girl, 'Give him honey to drink.' I said, 'I am fasting.' She said, 'Allah the Exalted has forbidden fasting on this day,' and this verse was revealed concerning it: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾."

Ibn Manjawayh narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abi Mulayka informed me that Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr informed them: "A caravan of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Bakr said, 'Appoint al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad as their leader,' and Umar said, 'Rather, appoint al-Aqra' ibn Habis.' Abu Bakr said, 'You only wanted to oppose me,' and Umar said, 'I did not want to oppose you.' They argued until their voices were raised, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾ ... to the end of the verse." [61] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/6 and Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/116, Dar al-Fikr edition.]]

Qatada said: "It was revealed concerning people who used to say, 'If only something had been revealed about such-and-such, such-and-such would be decided.' Allah disliked that, and He put forward [the matter]." Mujahid said: "Do not forestall [lā tafṭatū]" [[Lā tafṭatū: do not innovate in speech and issue rulings by your own opinion.]] "the Messenger of Allah in anything until Allah decides it on his tongue." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/150.]]

Al-Dahhak said: "It means in fighting and in the laws of the religion. He says: Do not decide a matter apart from Allah and His Messenger." Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: "Do not outrun the Messenger of Allah with a word or an action until he is the one who orders you." Al-Suddi also said this.

Ata al-Khurasani said: "It was revealed concerning the incident of Bi'r Ma'una." It was also said: "It was revealed concerning the three men who saved the two men of Sulaym, who had sought protection with Banu Amir, and who took their property, though they were people of a covenant. When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the news had already reached him, and he said, 'What a bad thing you have done! They are people of my covenant, and this one who is with you is one of my women [[As in the manuscript.]].' They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, they claimed that they were from Banu Amir, so we said, "They are two men from those who killed our brothers."' We said, 'They are for that.' The Sulaymites came to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'There is no retaliation for them, because they sought protection with our enemy.' But he supported them [[As in the manuscript.]], and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with them. Allah the Exalted revealed concerning that: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾, when they killed the two men." This is the narration of Madhan from Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Zayd said: "Do not cut off a matter apart from the Messenger of Allah." It was also said: "Do not walk in front of the Messenger of Allah, and likewise in front of the scholars, for they are the heirs of the prophets."

The evidence for this interpretation is what:

Abu al-Hasan al-Khabbazi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Musa ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari, there, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: A man in Mecca narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) saw me walking in front of Abu Bakr, and said, 'You walk in front of one who is better than you in this world and the Hereafter. The sun has not risen nor set upon anyone, after the Prophet (ﷺ) and the messengers, better or more excellent than Abu Bakr!!'" [63] [[Tarikh Baghdad: 14/379.]]

It was also said: It was revealed concerning people who used to attend the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whenever the Messenger was asked about something, they would plunge into it and put forward their speech and their opinions, so they were forbidden from that and warned against saying anything about any matter of the religion of Allah the Exalted before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said it.

It was also said: "Do not seek a rank beyond his rank." Al-Akhfash said: "The Arabs say: So-and-so went ahead before his father and his mother," and "he goes ahead when he takes a matter on his own, apart from them both." ﴿And fear Allah﴾ by neglecting His right and opposing His command. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾ of your words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of your deeds and your states.

﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ The verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who had a deafness in his ear and was loud-voiced. Whenever he spoke to someone, he raised his voice, and he would sometimes speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and call out loudly. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾, meaning: do not be harsh with him in address, and do not call him by his name, "O Muhammad, O Ahmad," as some of you call others, but honor him, respect him, and speak to him gently and kindly, with glorification and reverence: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 63.]].

﴿Lest your deeds be nullified﴾, that is, lest your good deeds be made void. The Arabs say: "The wall leaned [asnada al-ha'it] that it would fall." ﴿while you do not perceive.﴾

When this verse was revealed, Thabit sat on the road. Asim ibn Adi passed by him and said, "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said, "This verse; I fear it was revealed concerning me, for I have a loud voice, and I fear my deeds will be nullified and that I will be among the people of the Fire." Asim went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while Thabit was overcome with weeping. Then he came to his wife Jamila bint Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and said to her, "When you enter the house of my horse, fasten the wooden peg with a nail," and she did so. Then he came out and said, "I will not come out until Allah takes my soul, or the Messenger of Allah is pleased with me." Asim came to the Messenger of Allah and informed him of his situation. He said, "Go and call him to me." Asim went to the place where he had seen him but did not find him, so he went to his family and found him in the horse's stall. He said to him, "The Messenger of Allah is calling you." Thabit said, "Break the peg." They both came to the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said, "I am loud-voiced, and I fear this verse was revealed concerning me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "Are you not pleased to live happily, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise?" [64] [[Fath al-Bari: 6/457.]] He said, "I am pleased with the good news of Allah and His Messenger. I will never raise my voice again above the voice of the Messenger of Allah." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/153.]]

Anas said: "We used to look at a man of the people of Paradise walking before us. When it was the day of Yamama, in the war against Musaylima, Thabit saw some breaking among the Muslims, and a group of them fled. He said, 'Shame on these people, and what they are doing!' Then Thabit said to Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, 'We never fought the enemies of Allah with the Messenger of Allah like this.' Then they both stood firm and kept fighting until they were killed. Thabit ibn Qays was wearing armor. A man from the Companions saw him after his death in a dream, and he said to him: 'Know that so-and-so, a man from the Muslims, took my armor and went off with it. It is in a corner of the camp, beside a horse tethered by its long rope, and it has been placed over my armor, [covered with] his blood [[As in the manuscript; perhaps: his blood.]]. Go to Khalid ibn al-Walid and inform him, so that he returns my armor to me. Go to Abu Bakr, the caliph of the Messenger of Allah, and tell him: I have a debt that must be paid, and so-and-so, one of my slaves, is to be freed.'" The man informed Khalid, and he found the armor and the horse as described. He recovered the armor, and Khalid informed Abu Bakr of the dream, and Abu Bakr carried out his bequest. Malik ibn Anas said: "I do not know of any bequest being carried out after its maker's death except this one."

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhallidi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam, Yazid ibn Harun and Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salama, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "When ﴿do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said, 'By Allah, I will not raise my voice except as one who speaks in a low voice to a confidant [[Al-sirar: whispering; i.e., like one who whispers (Lisan al-Arab 4/362).]].'"

Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated from Abu al-Zubayr, who said: "When this verse was revealed, Umar did not speak to the Prophet (ﷺ) after that without the Prophet (ﷺ) having to ask him to repeat what he said because his voice was so low." So Allah the Exalted revealed concerning them: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, out of reverence for him, those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, that is, tested them, purified them, and chosen them, as gold is tested by fire so that its pure part emerges. Ibn Abbas said: "He honored them."

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl al-Nisaburi narrated to us, saying: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Khaythama narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Khawlaji, who said: I heard Abu Sulayman say: Umar ibn al-Khattab said, concerning ﴿those whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, "He removed desires from them." ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. It is said that these four verses, from His saying ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices...﴾ to His saying ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, were revealed concerning the delegation of Tamim.

This is what:

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Hani al-Warraq narrated to me in the year 337 AH, saying: al-Fadl ibn Muhammad ibn al-Musayyib ibn Musa al-Sha'rani narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Mu'alla ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far ibn Umar ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "The Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and called out at the door, 'O Muhammad, come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace.' The Prophet (ﷺ) heard them and came out to them, saying, 'That is only Allah, whose praise is an adornment and whose blame is a disgrace.'" [[Asbab al-Nuzul al-Ayat: 259.]]

They said: "We are people of Banu Tamim. We have come with our poet and our orator, to compete with you in poetry and boast against you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not sent with poetry, nor was I commanded to boast. But bring forward [your speaker]." [65] [[Asbab al-Nuzul al-Wahidi: 259.]]

Al-Zibriqan ibn Badr said to a young man among them: "Stand up and mention your virtue and the virtue of your people." He stood and said:

"Praise be to Allah, who made us the best of His creation and gave us wealth to spend as we wish. We are among the best people on earth, the most numerous in men, wealth and weapons. Whoever denies our words, let him bring a statement better than ours and deeds better than our deeds."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was the orator of the Messenger of Allah: "Stand up and answer him." He stood and said: "Praise be to Allah. I praise Him, seek His help, believe in Him, rely upon Him, and bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." Then he called upon the emigrants of his paternal cousins, the most handsome of people in appearance and the greatest in forbearance. They answered him and said: "Praise be to Allah, who made us His helpers, the ministers of His Messenger, and a might for His religion. We fight the people until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it, we protect his property and his life from us, and whoever refuses, we kill him, and his claim against Allah is light for us. I say my word, and I ask Allah's forgiveness for the believing men and the believing women."

Al-Zibriqan ibn Badr said to a young man among them: "Stand up, so-and-so, and recite some verses mentioning your virtue and the virtue of your people." The young man stood and said:

"We are the noble; no tribe can equal us.
Among us are the chiefs, and among us is the one who divides the quarter-share [[Al-mirba': the one-quarter share of booty taken by the chief.]].
We feed people in times of drought, all of them,
with the fat of the hump when the cloud brings no rain.
When we refuse, no one dares refuse us;
thus, when boasting, we rise high."

He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Hassan ibn Thabit, and the messenger went to him. He said, 'What do you want from me, when I was with him?' He said, 'The Banu Tamim have come with their poet and their orator. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Thabit ibn Qays to answer him, and their poet has spoken, so he has sent for you to answer him.'" He mentioned to him the words of their poet. He said: "Hassan came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to answer him. He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, have him let me hear what he said.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Let him recite to you what he said.' So he recited what he had said to him, and Hassan said:

"The lineage of Fihr and their brethren
have set a sunnah for the people that is followed.
Whoever's inner nature is pleased by it,
has piety toward Allah, and seeks all good."

Then Hassan said:

"We helped the Messenger of Allah and the religion by force,
despite the disdain of the arrogant of Mu'add and Hadir.
With blows like the spurting of milk from the udders of she-camels,
and thrusts like the mouths of the milk-camels that come forth."

"Ask anyone on the day when its mountain paths were thronged
with blows from us like lions in battle.
Do we not plunge into death in the thick of war
when the arrival of death between the armies is sweet?
We strike the heads of the armored, and we belong
to a noble lineage, the root of Ghassan, the conqueror.
Were it not for the shame before Allah, we would say, out of generosity
toward the people at the two sanctuaries [al-Khayfayn], is there any rival?
Our living are the best of those who have trodden the pebbles,
and our dead are the best of the people of the graveyards."

He said: "Al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood and said: 'By Allah, I came for a matter that these men did not come for, and I have composed some poetry; hear it from me.' He said, 'Speak.' He said:

"We came to you so that people might know our excellence
when they dispute with us at the mention of noble deeds.
We are the chiefs of the people of every tribe,
and there is none in the land of the Hijaz like the Darim [[The Darim: a branch of Tamim.]].
We have the quarter-share in every raid
that takes place in Najd or in the lowlands of Tihama."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Stand up, O Hassan, and answer him." Hassan stood and said:

"Banu Darim, do not boast; your boasting
will return as a disaster at the mention of noble deeds.
You were confounded that you would boast over us, while you
are, for us, servants, among nursing-mothers and servants."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You were rich, O brother of Darim, that what you were supposed to be remembered for, people had forgotten."

Thus the words of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were harder on them than the words of Hassan. Then Hassan returned to his poetry.

He said:

"Like the best of what you have attained of glory and eminence is our following after the mention of the noble ones,
So if you came seeking to preserve your blood and your wealth, that you not be divided in the shares,
Then do not set up a rival to God, and submit, and do not boast before the Prophet of your forefather Dārim,
Otherwise, by the Lord of the House, our hands will incline upon your heads with the keen, cutting swords."

He said: Then al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood up and said: "Indeed, Muhammad is the one who is to be obeyed (al-mawla). By God, I do not know what this affair is. Our orator spoke, and their orator was better in speech; and our poet spoke, and their poet was more eloquent and better in speech."

Then he drew near to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that you are His Messenger."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What was before this does not harm you." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave them and clothed them. He had been appointing (someone) to tend their mounts, namely ʿAmr ibn al-Ahtam, and Qays ibn ʿĀṣim hated him because of his youth. The Messenger of God gave him the same as he had given the people, so Qays disparaged him, composed verses of poetry against him, the voices rose, and the clamour grew before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Then God the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ up to His words ﴿and a great reward﴾, meaning abundant recompense, which is Paradise.

[[Its full text is in Asbab al-Nuzul: 259, and Tarikh Dimashq: 9/188–191 (ed. Dar al-Fikr), and Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 7/178.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Khabbazi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Musa ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari, there, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: A man in Mecca narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) saw me walking in front of Abu Bakr, and said, 'You walk in front of one who is better than you in this world and the Hereafter. The sun has not risen nor set upon anyone, after the Prophet (ﷺ) and the messengers, better or more excellent than Abu Bakr!!'" [63] [[Tarikh Baghdad: 14/379.]]

It was also said: It was revealed concerning people who used to attend the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whenever the Messenger was asked about something, they would plunge into it and put forward their speech and their opinions, so they were forbidden from that and warned against saying anything about any matter of the religion of Allah the Exalted before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said it.

It was also said: "Do not seek a rank beyond his rank." Al-Akhfash said: "The Arabs say: So-and-so went ahead before his father and his mother," and "he goes ahead when he takes a matter on his own, apart from them both." ﴿And fear Allah﴾ by neglecting His right and opposing His command. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾ of your words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of your deeds and your states.

﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ The verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who had a deafness in his ear and was loud-voiced. Whenever he spoke to someone, he raised his voice, and he would sometimes speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and call out loudly. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾, meaning: do not be harsh with him in address, and do not call him by his name, "O Muhammad, O Ahmad," as some of you call others, but honor him, respect him, and speak to him gently and kindly, with glorification and reverence: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 63.]].

﴿Lest your deeds be nullified﴾, that is, lest your good deeds be made void. The Arabs say: "The wall leaned [asnada al-ha'it] that it would fall." ﴿while you do not perceive.﴾

When this verse was revealed, Thabit sat on the road. Asim ibn Adi passed by him and said, "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said, "This verse; I fear it was revealed concerning me, for I have a loud voice, and I fear my deeds will be nullified and that I will be among the people of the Fire." Asim went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while Thabit was overcome with weeping. Then he came to his wife Jamila bint Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and said to her, "When you enter the house of my horse, fasten the wooden peg with a nail," and she did so. Then he came out and said, "I will not come out until Allah takes my soul, or the Messenger of Allah is pleased with me." Asim came to the Messenger of Allah and informed him of his situation. He said, "Go and call him to me." Asim went to the place where he had seen him but did not find him, so he went to his family and found him in the horse's stall. He said to him, "The Messenger of Allah is calling you." Thabit said, "Break the peg." They both came to the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said, "I am loud-voiced, and I fear this verse was revealed concerning me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "Are you not pleased to live happily, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise?" [64] [[Fath al-Bari: 6/457.]] He said, "I am pleased with the good news of Allah and His Messenger. I will never raise my voice again above the voice of the Messenger of Allah." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/153.]]

Anas said: "We used to look at a man of the people of Paradise walking before us. When it was the day of Yamama, in the war against Musaylima, Thabit saw some breaking among the Muslims, and a group of them fled. He said, 'Shame on these people, and what they are doing!' Then Thabit said to Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, 'We never fought the enemies of Allah with the Messenger of Allah like this.' Then they both stood firm and kept fighting until they were killed. Thabit ibn Qays was wearing armor. A man from the Companions saw him after his death in a dream, and he said to him: 'Know that so-and-so, a man from the Muslims, took my armor and went off with it. It is in a corner of the camp, beside a horse tethered by its long rope, and it has been placed over my armor, [covered with] his blood [[As in the manuscript; perhaps: his blood.]]. Go to Khalid ibn al-Walid and inform him, so that he returns my armor to me. Go to Abu Bakr, the caliph of the Messenger of Allah, and tell him: I have a debt that must be paid, and so-and-so, one of my slaves, is to be freed.'" The man informed Khalid, and he found the armor and the horse as described. He recovered the armor, and Khalid informed Abu Bakr of the dream, and Abu Bakr carried out his bequest. Malik ibn Anas said: "I do not know of any bequest being carried out after its maker's death except this one."

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhallidi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam, Yazid ibn Harun and Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salama, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "When ﴿do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said, 'By Allah, I will not raise my voice except as one who speaks in a low voice to a confidant [[Al-sirar: whispering; i.e., like one who whispers (Lisan al-Arab 4/362).]].'"

Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated from Abu al-Zubayr, who said: "When this verse was revealed, Umar did not speak to the Prophet (ﷺ) after that without the Prophet (ﷺ) having to ask him to repeat what he said because his voice was so low." So Allah the Exalted revealed concerning them: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, out of reverence for him, those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, that is, tested them, purified them, and chosen them, as gold is tested by fire so that its pure part emerges. Ibn Abbas said: "He honored them."

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl al-Nisaburi narrated to us, saying: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Khaythama narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Khawlaji, who said: I heard Abu Sulayman say: Umar ibn al-Khattab said, concerning ﴿those whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, "He removed desires from them." ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. It is said that these four verses, from His saying ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices...﴾ to His saying ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, were revealed concerning the delegation of Tamim.

This is what:

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Hani al-Warraq narrated to me in the year 337 AH, saying: al-Fadl ibn Muhammad ibn al-Musayyib ibn Musa al-Sha'rani narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Mu'alla ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far ibn Umar ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "The Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and called out at the door, 'O Muhammad, come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace.' The Prophet (ﷺ) heard them and came out to them, saying, 'That is only Allah, whose praise is an adornment and whose blame is a disgrace.'" [[Asbab al-Nuzul al-Ayat: 259.]]

They said: "We are people of Banu Tamim. We have come with our poet and our orator, to compete with you in poetry and boast against you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not sent with poetry, nor was I commanded to boast. But bring forward [your speaker]." [65] [[Asbab al-Nuzul al-Wahidi: 259.]]

Al-Zibriqan ibn Badr said to a young man among them: "Stand up and mention your virtue and the virtue of your people." He stood and said:

"Praise be to Allah, who made us the best of His creation and gave us wealth to spend as we wish. We are among the best people on earth, the most numerous in men, wealth and weapons. Whoever denies our words, let him bring a statement better than ours and deeds better than our deeds."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was the orator of the Messenger of Allah: "Stand up and answer him." He stood and said: "Praise be to Allah. I praise Him, seek His help, believe in Him, rely upon Him, and bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." Then he called upon the emigrants of his paternal cousins, the most handsome of people in appearance and the greatest in forbearance. They answered him and said: "Praise be to Allah, who made us His helpers, the ministers of His Messenger, and a might for His religion. We fight the people until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it, we protect his property and his life from us, and whoever refuses, we kill him, and his claim against Allah is light for us. I say my word, and I ask Allah's forgiveness for the believing men and the believing women."

Al-Zibriqan ibn Badr said to a young man among them: "Stand up, so-and-so, and recite some verses mentioning your virtue and the virtue of your people." The young man stood and said:

"We are the noble; no tribe can equal us.
Among us are the chiefs, and among us is the one who divides the quarter-share [[Al-mirba': the one-quarter share of booty taken by the chief.]].
We feed people in times of drought, all of them,
with the fat of the hump when the cloud brings no rain.
When we refuse, no one dares refuse us;
thus, when boasting, we rise high."

He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Hassan ibn Thabit, and the messenger went to him. He said, 'What do you want from me, when I was with him?' He said, 'The Banu Tamim have come with their poet and their orator. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Thabit ibn Qays to answer him, and their poet has spoken, so he has sent for you to answer him.'" He mentioned to him the words of their poet. He said: "Hassan came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to answer him. He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, have him let me hear what he said.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Let him recite to you what he said.' So he recited what he had said to him, and Hassan said:

"The lineage of Fihr and their brethren
have set a sunnah for the people that is followed.
Whoever's inner nature is pleased by it,
has piety toward Allah, and seeks all good."

Then Hassan said:

"We helped the Messenger of Allah and the religion by force,
despite the disdain of the arrogant of Mu'add and Hadir.
With blows like the spurting of milk from the udders of she-camels,
and thrusts like the mouths of the milk-camels that come forth."

"Ask anyone on the day when its mountain paths were thronged
with blows from us like lions in battle.
Do we not plunge into death in the thick of war
when the arrival of death between the armies is sweet?
We strike the heads of the armored, and we belong
to a noble lineage, the root of Ghassan, the conqueror.
Were it not for the shame before Allah, we would say, out of generosity
toward the people at the two sanctuaries [al-Khayfayn], is there any rival?
Our living are the best of those who have trodden the pebbles,
and our dead are the best of the people of the graveyards."

He said: "Al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood and said: 'By Allah, I came for a matter that these men did not come for, and I have composed some poetry; hear it from me.' He said, 'Speak.' He said:

"We came to you so that people might know our excellence
when they dispute with us at the mention of noble deeds.
We are the chiefs of the people of every tribe,
and there is none in the land of the Hijaz like the Darim [[The Darim: a branch of Tamim.]].
We have the quarter-share in every raid
that takes place in Najd or in the lowlands of Tihama."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Stand up, O Hassan, and answer him." Hassan stood and said:

"Banu Darim, do not boast; your boasting
will return as a disaster at the mention of noble deeds.
You were confounded that you would boast over us, while you
are, for us, servants, among nursing-mothers and servants."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You were rich, O brother of Darim, that what you were supposed to be remembered for, people had forgotten."

Thus the words of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were harder on them than the words of Hassan. Then Hassan returned to his poetry.

He said:

"Like the best of what you have attained of glory and eminence is our following after the mention of the noble ones,
So if you came seeking to preserve your blood and your wealth, that you not be divided in the shares,
Then do not set up a rival to God, and submit, and do not boast before the Prophet of your forefather Dārim,
Otherwise, by the Lord of the House, our hands will incline upon your heads with the keen, cutting swords."

He said: Then al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood up and said: "Indeed, Muhammad is the one who is to be obeyed (al-mawla). By God, I do not know what this affair is. Our orator spoke, and their orator was better in speech; and our poet spoke, and their poet was more eloquent and better in speech."

Then he drew near to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that you are His Messenger."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What was before this does not harm you." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave them and clothed them. He had been appointing (someone) to tend their mounts, namely ʿAmr ibn al-Ahtam, and Qays ibn ʿĀṣim hated him because of his youth. The Messenger of God gave him the same as he had given the people, so Qays disparaged him, composed verses of poetry against him, the voices rose, and the clamour grew before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Then God the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ up to His words ﴿and a great reward﴾, meaning abundant recompense, which is Paradise.

[[Its full text is in Asbab al-Nuzul: 259, and Tarikh Dimashq: 9/188–191 (ed. Dar al-Fikr), and Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 7/178.]]

Sura 49 (al-Hujurat), Madaniyya (Medinan). It has 1,475 letters, 343 words, and 18 verses.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Abdawi narrated to us, reading it to him in the year 384 AH. He said: Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Adl narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym al-Mada'ini narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites al-Hujurat will be given ten good deeds for each person who obeyed Allah and each person who disobeyed Him." [60] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/214.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger.﴾ The majority of reciters read ﴿tuqaddimu﴾ with a dammah on the ta' and a kasrah on the dal, from taqdim (putting forward). Al-Dahhak and Ya'qub read it with a fathah on both, from taqaddum (going forward). The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Do not speak contrary to the Book and the Sunnah."

Atiyya narrated from him: "Do not speak before his speech."

Abd Allah ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Umar ibn al-Hasan ibn Malik al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id ibn Uthman al-Khazzaz narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn Mahariq Abu Janada narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Salama, from al-Sab'i, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, concerning ﴿do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾, that it refers to the slaughtering on the day of al-Adha (Eid al-Adha). Al-Hasan held this view and said: "Do not slaughter before the Prophet (ﷺ) slaughters. Some Muslims slaughtered before the Prophet's (ﷺ) prayer, so he ordered them to repeat the slaughter."

Abd al-Khaliq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Hayy narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Awwam al-Riyahi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: al-Nu'man ibn Abd al-Salam al-Taymi narrated to us, from Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl, from Yahya ibn Abd Allah al-Taymi, from Habbal ibn Rufayda, from Masruq, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), concerning His saying ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾, she said: "Do not fast before your Prophet fasts."

It was also narrated from Masruq: "I entered upon Aisha on the day I came [to her], and she said to the slave-girl, 'Give him honey to drink.' I said, 'I am fasting.' She said, 'Allah the Exalted has forbidden fasting on this day,' and this verse was revealed concerning it: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾."

Ibn Manjawayh narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abi Mulayka informed me that Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr informed them: "A caravan of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ). Abu Bakr said, 'Appoint al-Qa'qa' ibn Ma'bad as their leader,' and Umar said, 'Rather, appoint al-Aqra' ibn Habis.' Abu Bakr said, 'You only wanted to oppose me,' and Umar said, 'I did not want to oppose you.' They argued until their voices were raised, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾ ... to the end of the verse." [61] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/6 and Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/116, Dar al-Fikr edition.]]

Qatada said: "It was revealed concerning people who used to say, 'If only something had been revealed about such-and-such, such-and-such would be decided.' Allah disliked that, and He put forward [the matter]." Mujahid said: "Do not forestall [lā tafṭatū]" [[Lā tafṭatū: do not innovate in speech and issue rulings by your own opinion.]] "the Messenger of Allah in anything until Allah decides it on his tongue." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/150.]]

Al-Dahhak said: "It means in fighting and in the laws of the religion. He says: Do not decide a matter apart from Allah and His Messenger." Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: "Do not outrun the Messenger of Allah with a word or an action until he is the one who orders you." Al-Suddi also said this.

Ata al-Khurasani said: "It was revealed concerning the incident of Bi'r Ma'una." It was also said: "It was revealed concerning the three men who saved the two men of Sulaym, who had sought protection with Banu Amir, and who took their property, though they were people of a covenant. When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the news had already reached him, and he said, 'What a bad thing you have done! They are people of my covenant, and this one who is with you is one of my women [[As in the manuscript.]].' They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, they claimed that they were from Banu Amir, so we said, "They are two men from those who killed our brothers."' We said, 'They are for that.' The Sulaymites came to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'There is no retaliation for them, because they sought protection with our enemy.' But he supported them [[As in the manuscript.]], and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made peace with them. Allah the Exalted revealed concerning that: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] forward before Allah and His Messenger﴾, when they killed the two men." This is the narration of Madhan from Ibn Abbas.

Ibn Zayd said: "Do not cut off a matter apart from the Messenger of Allah." It was also said: "Do not walk in front of the Messenger of Allah, and likewise in front of the scholars, for they are the heirs of the prophets."

The evidence for this interpretation is what:

Abu al-Hasan al-Khabbazi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Musa ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari, there, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: A man in Mecca narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) saw me walking in front of Abu Bakr, and said, 'You walk in front of one who is better than you in this world and the Hereafter. The sun has not risen nor set upon anyone, after the Prophet (ﷺ) and the messengers, better or more excellent than Abu Bakr!!'" [63] [[Tarikh Baghdad: 14/379.]]

It was also said: It was revealed concerning people who used to attend the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whenever the Messenger was asked about something, they would plunge into it and put forward their speech and their opinions, so they were forbidden from that and warned against saying anything about any matter of the religion of Allah the Exalted before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said it.

It was also said: "Do not seek a rank beyond his rank." Al-Akhfash said: "The Arabs say: So-and-so went ahead before his father and his mother," and "he goes ahead when he takes a matter on his own, apart from them both." ﴿And fear Allah﴾ by neglecting His right and opposing His command. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾ of your words, ﴿Knowing﴾ of your deeds and your states.

﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ The verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who had a deafness in his ear and was loud-voiced. Whenever he spoke to someone, he raised his voice, and he would sometimes speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and call out loudly. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾, meaning: do not be harsh with him in address, and do not call him by his name, "O Muhammad, O Ahmad," as some of you call others, but honor him, respect him, and speak to him gently and kindly, with glorification and reverence: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 63.]].

﴿Lest your deeds be nullified﴾, that is, lest your good deeds be made void. The Arabs say: "The wall leaned [asnada al-ha'it] that it would fall." ﴿while you do not perceive.﴾

When this verse was revealed, Thabit sat on the road. Asim ibn Adi passed by him and said, "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said, "This verse; I fear it was revealed concerning me, for I have a loud voice, and I fear my deeds will be nullified and that I will be among the people of the Fire." Asim went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while Thabit was overcome with weeping. Then he came to his wife Jamila bint Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and said to her, "When you enter the house of my horse, fasten the wooden peg with a nail," and she did so. Then he came out and said, "I will not come out until Allah takes my soul, or the Messenger of Allah is pleased with me." Asim came to the Messenger of Allah and informed him of his situation. He said, "Go and call him to me." Asim went to the place where he had seen him but did not find him, so he went to his family and found him in the horse's stall. He said to him, "The Messenger of Allah is calling you." Thabit said, "Break the peg." They both came to the Messenger of Allah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "What makes you weep, O Thabit?" He said, "I am loud-voiced, and I fear this verse was revealed concerning me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "Are you not pleased to live happily, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise?" [64] [[Fath al-Bari: 6/457.]] He said, "I am pleased with the good news of Allah and His Messenger. I will never raise my voice again above the voice of the Messenger of Allah." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/153.]]

Anas said: "We used to look at a man of the people of Paradise walking before us. When it was the day of Yamama, in the war against Musaylima, Thabit saw some breaking among the Muslims, and a group of them fled. He said, 'Shame on these people, and what they are doing!' Then Thabit said to Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, 'We never fought the enemies of Allah with the Messenger of Allah like this.' Then they both stood firm and kept fighting until they were killed. Thabit ibn Qays was wearing armor. A man from the Companions saw him after his death in a dream, and he said to him: 'Know that so-and-so, a man from the Muslims, took my armor and went off with it. It is in a corner of the camp, beside a horse tethered by its long rope, and it has been placed over my armor, [covered with] his blood [[As in the manuscript; perhaps: his blood.]]. Go to Khalid ibn al-Walid and inform him, so that he returns my armor to me. Go to Abu Bakr, the caliph of the Messenger of Allah, and tell him: I have a debt that must be paid, and so-and-so, one of my slaves, is to be freed.'" The man informed Khalid, and he found the armor and the horse as described. He recovered the armor, and Khalid informed Abu Bakr of the dream, and Abu Bakr carried out his bequest. Malik ibn Anas said: "I do not know of any bequest being carried out after its maker's death except this one."

Abu Muhammad al-Mukhallidi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam, Yazid ibn Harun and Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salama, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "When ﴿do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet...﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said, 'By Allah, I will not raise my voice except as one who speaks in a low voice to a confidant [[Al-sirar: whispering; i.e., like one who whispers (Lisan al-Arab 4/362).]].'"

Ibn Abi Mulayka narrated from Abu al-Zubayr, who said: "When this verse was revealed, Umar did not speak to the Prophet (ﷺ) after that without the Prophet (ﷺ) having to ask him to repeat what he said because his voice was so low." So Allah the Exalted revealed concerning them: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, out of reverence for him, those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, that is, tested them, purified them, and chosen them, as gold is tested by fire so that its pure part emerges. Ibn Abbas said: "He honored them."

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl al-Nisaburi narrated to us, saying: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Khaythama narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi al-Khawlaji, who said: I heard Abu Sulayman say: Umar ibn al-Khattab said, concerning ﴿those whose hearts Allah has tested for piety﴾, "He removed desires from them." ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. It is said that these four verses, from His saying ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices...﴾ to His saying ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, were revealed concerning the delegation of Tamim.

This is what:

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Hani al-Warraq narrated to me in the year 337 AH, saying: al-Fadl ibn Muhammad ibn al-Musayyib ibn Musa al-Sha'rani narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Mu'alla ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far ibn Umar ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "The Banu Tamim came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and called out at the door, 'O Muhammad, come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace.' The Prophet (ﷺ) heard them and came out to them, saying, 'That is only Allah, whose praise is an adornment and whose blame is a disgrace.'" [[Asbab al-Nuzul al-Ayat: 259.]]

They said: "We are people of Banu Tamim. We have come with our poet and our orator, to compete with you in poetry and boast against you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not sent with poetry, nor was I commanded to boast. But bring forward [your speaker]." [65] [[Asbab al-Nuzul al-Wahidi: 259.]]

Al-Zibriqan ibn Badr said to a young man among them: "Stand up and mention your virtue and the virtue of your people." He stood and said:

"Praise be to Allah, who made us the best of His creation and gave us wealth to spend as we wish. We are among the best people on earth, the most numerous in men, wealth and weapons. Whoever denies our words, let him bring a statement better than ours and deeds better than our deeds."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was the orator of the Messenger of Allah: "Stand up and answer him." He stood and said: "Praise be to Allah. I praise Him, seek His help, believe in Him, rely upon Him, and bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." Then he called upon the emigrants of his paternal cousins, the most handsome of people in appearance and the greatest in forbearance. They answered him and said: "Praise be to Allah, who made us His helpers, the ministers of His Messenger, and a might for His religion. We fight the people until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah. Whoever says it, we protect his property and his life from us, and whoever refuses, we kill him, and his claim against Allah is light for us. I say my word, and I ask Allah's forgiveness for the believing men and the believing women."

Al-Zibriqan ibn Badr said to a young man among them: "Stand up, so-and-so, and recite some verses mentioning your virtue and the virtue of your people." The young man stood and said:

"We are the noble; no tribe can equal us.
Among us are the chiefs, and among us is the one who divides the quarter-share [[Al-mirba': the one-quarter share of booty taken by the chief.]].
We feed people in times of drought, all of them,
with the fat of the hump when the cloud brings no rain.
When we refuse, no one dares refuse us;
thus, when boasting, we rise high."

He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Hassan ibn Thabit, and the messenger went to him. He said, 'What do you want from me, when I was with him?' He said, 'The Banu Tamim have come with their poet and their orator. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Thabit ibn Qays to answer him, and their poet has spoken, so he has sent for you to answer him.'" He mentioned to him the words of their poet. He said: "Hassan came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to answer him. He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, have him let me hear what he said.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Let him recite to you what he said.' So he recited what he had said to him, and Hassan said:

"The lineage of Fihr and their brethren
have set a sunnah for the people that is followed.
Whoever's inner nature is pleased by it,
has piety toward Allah, and seeks all good."

Then Hassan said:

"We helped the Messenger of Allah and the religion by force,
despite the disdain of the arrogant of Mu'add and Hadir.
With blows like the spurting of milk from the udders of she-camels,
and thrusts like the mouths of the milk-camels that come forth."

"Ask anyone on the day when its mountain paths were thronged
with blows from us like lions in battle.
Do we not plunge into death in the thick of war
when the arrival of death between the armies is sweet?
We strike the heads of the armored, and we belong
to a noble lineage, the root of Ghassan, the conqueror.
Were it not for the shame before Allah, we would say, out of generosity
toward the people at the two sanctuaries [al-Khayfayn], is there any rival?
Our living are the best of those who have trodden the pebbles,
and our dead are the best of the people of the graveyards."

He said: "Al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood and said: 'By Allah, I came for a matter that these men did not come for, and I have composed some poetry; hear it from me.' He said, 'Speak.' He said:

"We came to you so that people might know our excellence
when they dispute with us at the mention of noble deeds.
We are the chiefs of the people of every tribe,
and there is none in the land of the Hijaz like the Darim [[The Darim: a branch of Tamim.]].
We have the quarter-share in every raid
that takes place in Najd or in the lowlands of Tihama."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Stand up, O Hassan, and answer him." Hassan stood and said:

"Banu Darim, do not boast; your boasting
will return as a disaster at the mention of noble deeds.
You were confounded that you would boast over us, while you
are, for us, servants, among nursing-mothers and servants."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You were rich, O brother of Darim, that what you were supposed to be remembered for, people had forgotten."

Thus the words of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were harder on them than the words of Hassan. Then Hassan returned to his poetry.

He said:

"Like the best of what you have attained of glory and eminence is our following after the mention of the noble ones,
So if you came seeking to preserve your blood and your wealth, that you not be divided in the shares,
Then do not set up a rival to God, and submit, and do not boast before the Prophet of your forefather Dārim,
Otherwise, by the Lord of the House, our hands will incline upon your heads with the keen, cutting swords."

He said: Then al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood up and said: "Indeed, Muhammad is the one who is to be obeyed (al-mawla). By God, I do not know what this affair is. Our orator spoke, and their orator was better in speech; and our poet spoke, and their poet was more eloquent and better in speech."

Then he drew near to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that you are His Messenger."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What was before this does not harm you." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave them and clothed them. He had been appointing (someone) to tend their mounts, namely ʿAmr ibn al-Ahtam, and Qays ibn ʿĀṣim hated him because of his youth. The Messenger of God gave him the same as he had given the people, so Qays disparaged him, composed verses of poetry against him, the voices rose, and the clamour grew before the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Then God the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾ up to His words ﴿and a great reward﴾, meaning abundant recompense, which is Paradise.

[[Its full text is in Asbab al-Nuzul: 259, and Tarikh Dimashq: 9/188–191 (ed. Dar al-Fikr), and Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 7/178.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 49, verses 4–10:

Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the apartments (﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِنْ وَراءِ الْحُجُراتِ﴾). He means the Bedouins of Tamim, who called out: "O Muhammad, come out to us, for our praise is an adornment and our blame is a disgrace." This was said by Qatadah.

Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a expedition to a clan of Banu al-Anbar and appointed over them ʿUyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari. When they learned that he was heading toward them, they fled and left their dependents behind, so ʿUyaynah took them captive and brought them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Afterward their men came to ransom the children and women. They arrived at the time of midday heat and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) resting with his family. When the captives saw them, they rushed to their fathers, weeping. Each of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a house and a chamber, and they hastened to have the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) come out to them, and they began calling out: "O Muhammad, come out to us!" until they woke him from his sleep. He came out to them, and they said: "O Muhammad, release our dependents to us."

Then Jibril descended and said: "O Muhammad, Allah commands you to place between you and them a man." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Are you content that Samurah ibn Amr should be between me and you, and he is of your religion?"

They said: "Yes." Samurah said: "I will not judge between them, for my paternal uncle is a witness, and he is al-Aʿwar ibn Shamah." So they agreed to him.

Al-Aʿwar said: "I see that half of them should be ransomed and half should be freed." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am content."

So they ransomed half of them and freed half of them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever owes a freed person from the descendants of Ismaʿil, let him free some of them" [66] [[al-Muʿjam al-Kabir 10/185 – in the source the hadith reads thus: "Whoever owes a freed person from the descendants of Ismaʿil, let him not free anyone from Himyar." Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 10/46.]]. Then Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you...﴾, the verse.

Zayd ibn Arqam said: Some people from the upper rooms came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and some of them said to others: "Come, let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we are the happiest of people with him; and if he is a king, we will be supported in his shadow." So they came to the chamber of the Prophet (ﷺ) and began calling out to him: "O Muhammad! O Muhammad!" Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the apartments﴾.

The word (ḥujurāt) is the plural of ḥujr, and ḥujr is the plural of ḥujrah, so it is a plural of a plural. There are two readings: with a fatḥah on the jim, which is the reading of Abu Jaʿfar, as in the words of the poet:

Did not ʿAbbad, a protector for Darim, ... rule over them, and over the houses that have the apartments?

He means: rule over them, and over the Banu Hashim.

﴿Most of them are foolish and do not reason. And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them﴾, because you would have freed them all, releasing them without ransom. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿIsa ibn al-Sakkin al-Baladi narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani narrated to me, saying: Yaʿla ibn al-Ashdaq narrated to me, saying: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to me, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the apartments﴾. He said: "They are the boorish ones of Banu Tamim. Were it not that they are among the fiercest of people in fighting al-Aʿwar, the Dajjal, I would have asked Allah, mighty and majestic, to destroy them" [67] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/87.]].

﴿O you who have believed, if a debauched person comes to you with information...﴾, the verse.

It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him to Banu al-Mustaliq after the battle as a collector of zakat. There had been enmity between him and them in the pre-Islamic period. When the people heard of him, they went out to meet him, honoring the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Satan suggested to him that they intended to kill him, so he feared them and returned from the road to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Banu al-Mustaliq have withheld their charities and wanted to kill me." The Messenger was angry and resolved to raid them. The people learned of his return, so they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we heard of your messenger, so we went out to meet him, to honor him, and to pay him what we owed of Allah's right. Then he changed his mind about returning, and we feared that what turned him back from the road was a letter that came to him from you, due to an anger you felt toward us. We seek refuge in Allah from His anger and the anger of His Messenger." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left them undetermined [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir (4/224): and the Prophet sought to test them and resolved against them, so Allah revealed their excuse.]], and he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to them secretly with an army, and commanded him to conceal his arrival from them [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/161.]].

He said to him: "Observe. If you see from them what indicates their faith, then take from them the zakat of their wealth. If you do not see that, then treat them as one would treat the disbelievers."

Khalid did so and reached them, and he heard from them the call to prayer for Maghrib and ʿIshaʾ. He took their charities, and he saw from them nothing but obedience and goodness. Khalid returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the matter. Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, if a debauched person comes to you with information﴾, meaning al-Walid ibn ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt.

Allah named him a debauched person (fāsiq). Its parallel is: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is a debauched? They are not equal﴾ [[Surah al-Sajdah: 18.]]. Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah and Ibn Zayd said: the fāsiq is the liar. Abu al-Husayn al-Warraq said: he is one who openly commits sin. Ibn Tahir and Ibn Zayd said: the fāsiq is one who is not ashamed before Allah, glorified is He.

(bi-naba'): with information. ﴿Then verify, lest you harm a people in ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful﴾, that is, lest you harm them by killing and fighting. ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾, so be wary of saying falsehood and fabricating lies, for Allah, glorified is He, informs him of your reports and makes him aware of your conditions, and you would be exposed. ﴿Were he to obey you in much of the matter﴾, by judging by your opinion and accepting your words, ﴿you would surely be in difficulty﴾, that is, you would sin and be ruined. ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it beautiful in your hearts, and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance, and disobedience﴾. So you obey the Messenger of Allah and follow him, and Allah protects you from that difficulty by this.

Then He moved from address to narration, saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the rightly guided﴾. Its parallel is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And what you give in zakat, seeking the Face of Allah — those are the ones who receive multiplied reward﴾ [[Surah al-Rum: 39.]]. Al-Nabighah said:

O Dariyyah, at al-ʿAliyah and al-Sanad, ... they have become desolate, and the ancient ages have lengthened over them.

﴿As a bounty﴾, meaning this was a bounty ﴿from Allah and a favor, and Allah is Knowing, Wise.﴾

﴿And if two groups of the believers fight...﴾

Most of the exegetes said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once passed by a gathering of the Ansar while he was on his donkey, and the donkey urinated. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy held his nose and said: "Get away from us with your donkey, for its stench has harmed us." ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawahah said: "By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is sweeter in scent than you."

A man of the people of Ibn Ubayy grew angry for him, and a man of the people of Ibn Rawahah grew angry for him, so the companions of each of them grew angry until they insulted one another and struck each other with hands, palm fronds, and sandals. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could not restrain them, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it, and they reconciled and refrained from one another. Bashir ibn al-Nuʿman al-Ansari came, wrapped in his sword, and found them reconciled. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "Do you wrap yourself in the sword over me, O Bashir?" He said: "Yes, by the One I swear by, if you had come before you reconciled, I would have struck you until I killed you." Then ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy began to say:

Whenever your master is your adversary in struggle, ... you are humbled, and those you wrestle with overcome you.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning two men of the Ansar who had a dispute over a right between them. One of them said to the other: "I will certainly take my right from you by force, because of the multitude of my clan." The other called him to be judged before the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), but he refused to follow him. The matter between them continued until they pushed one another, and they had struck each other with hands and sandals, but there was no fighting with swords.

Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated from al-Kalbi that it was revealed concerning the war between Samir and Hatib. Samir had killed Hatib, so the Aws and the Khazraj fought until the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, and Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse and commanded His Prophet and the believers to reconcile between them.

Sufyan narrated from al-Suddi, who said: There was a woman of the Ansar called Umm Zayd, who was under a man, and something had happened between her and her husband. He threw her into an upper room and confined her there. Her people heard of it and came, and his people came, and they fought with hands and sandals. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight﴾, the verse.

﴿So reconcile between them﴾ by calling them to the judgment of the Book of Allah, glorified is He, and by their acceptance of what is in it for them and against them.

﴿But if one of them transgresses against the other, then fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah﴾, that is, refuses to accept the judgment of Allah, the Exalted, in its favor or against it, in His Book which He made a standard between His creation. ﴿And if it returns﴾, that is, returns to the truth, ﴿then reconcile between them with justice﴾, by urging them toward fairness and acceptance of the judgment of Allah, which is justice. ﴿And act justly; indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾

﴿The believers are but brothers﴾ in religion and allegiance. ﴿So make reconciliation between your two brothers﴾ when they disagree and fight. Ibn Sirin and Yaʿqub read: ﴿between your brothers﴾ (with ta') in the plural. al-Hasan read (ikhwanakum) with an alif and a nun. ﴿And fear Allah, that you may be given mercy.﴾ That is, do not disobey Him or oppose His command.

Abu ʿUthman al-Basri said: Brotherhood in religion is more firmly established than brotherhood by lineage, for brotherhood by lineage is severed by opposition in religion, but brotherhood in religion is not severed by opposition in lineage. Al-Junayd was asked about the brother, and he said: "He is you in reality, except that he is other than you in person."

Ibn Manjawayh informed me, saying: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mashuhi narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Rafi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Saʿid, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, nor belittle him, nor forsake him, nor exalt himself over him in building, so as to block the wind from him, except with his permission; nor harm him with the steam of his cooking pot unless he gives him some; nor buy fruit for his children, so that they go out with it to the children of his neighbor and do not give them any of it."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be mindful, and few of you will remember it" [68] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/323.]].

In these two verses is evidence that rebellion does not remove the name of faith, for Allah, glorified and exalted, called them brothers who are believers while they are rebels and disobedient. This is supported by what al-Aʿwar narrated: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, the exemplar in fighting the people of rebellion, was asked about the people of the Camel and Siffin: "Are they polytheists?" He said: "No, they fled from polytheism." It was asked: "Are they hypocrites?" He said: "Indeed, the hypocrites do not remember Allah except a little." It was asked: "Then what is their state?" He said: "They are our brothers who rebelled against us."

Ibn Manjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr al-Tammar narrated to us, saying: Kawthar narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O servant of Allah, do you know how Allah, glorified is He, judges those among this community who rebel?"

He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Their wounded are not to be finished off, their captives are not to be killed, their fugitives are not to be pursued, and their spoils are not to be divided" [69] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/320.]].

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi was asked about these two verses and said: The Prophet (ﷺ) made the reward of one who reconciles between people like the reward of one who fights in the way of Allah.

Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah said: Walk a mile and visit a sick person; walk two miles and reconcile between two people; walk three miles and visit your brother for the sake of Allah.

When the Prophet ﷺ finished the prayer, his companions took their seats [from him, so each man settled] in his own place, and hardly anyone would make room for another. Whenever a man came and found no seat, he would stand where he was. When Thabit finished the prayer and rose from it, he came toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, stepping over the people's necks and saying: "Make room, make room!" They began making room for him until he reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with one man between him and the Prophet.

[Thabit] said to him: "Make room." The man said to him: "You have found a seat, so sit down." Thabit sat behind him, angry. When the darkness had cleared, Thabit nudged the man and said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am so-and-so." Thabit said to him: "The son of such-and-such a woman," mentioning a mother of his for whom he used to be reproached in the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period). The man lowered his head in shame, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse.

Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning the delegation of Tamim whom we mentioned at the beginning of the surah. They mocked the poor companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, such as Ammar, Khabbab, Bilal, Suhayb, Salman, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfa, because of the shabbiness of their condition. Allah, glorified is He, then revealed, concerning those among them who had believed: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people﴾, meaning men [mocking] men. The word "qawm" (people) is a term that includes men and women, though it may also be specific to a group of men, as in the verse of Zuhayr:

"And I do not know—and soon I will know, I think— / whether the people of Hisn are men or women."

﴿…it may be that they are better than them; nor let women [ridicule] women, for it may be that they are better than them.﴾

It was revealed concerning two wives of the Prophet ﷺ who mocked Umm Salama. She had tied her waistband with a sabiba (a white cloth; the sabb is similar) and let its ends hang behind her, so she was dragging it. Aisha said to Hafsa: "Look at what she is dragging behind her; it is like a dog's tongue." That was their mockery.

Anas said: It was revealed concerning the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who reproached Umm Salama for being short. It is also said it was revealed concerning Aisha, who pointed with her hand at Umm Salama, [indicating] that she was short.

Ikrima narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "The women reproach me, saying: 'O Jewess, daughter of two Jews!'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Why did you not say: 'My father is Aaron, my paternal uncle is Moses, and my husband is Muhammad'?" Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

﴿And do not defame one another﴾, meaning: do not disparage one another, and do not attack one another. It is also said: "al-lamz" is faultfinding in someone's presence, and "al-hamz" is in his absence. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: "al-lamz" is with the tongue, the eye, and gestures, whereas "al-hamz" is only with the tongue. The poet said:

"When I meet you after a distance, you smile at me, / but when you are absent, you are the one who slanders and defames."

﴿And do not insult one another with nicknames﴾

Abu Jubayr ibn al-Dahhak said: This verse was revealed concerning us, the Banu Salama. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names. Whenever he called a man by one of them, we would say: "O Messenger of Allah, he gets angry at this name." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not insult one another with nicknames﴾.

Qatada and Ikrima said: It is a man's saying to another: "O sinner, O hypocrite, O unbeliever." Al-Hasan said: A Jew or a Christian would become Muslim, and then he would be called "O Jew" or "O Christian," so they were forbidden from this. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Insulting by nicknames" is when a man has committed evil deeds, then repented of them and returned to the truth, and Allah forbade that he be reproached for what he had done in the past.

﴿How evil is the name of wickedness after faith﴾. He means: whoever does what he has been forbidden—mockery, faultfinding, and insulting by nicknames—is a fasiq (wicked person). ﴿How evil is the name of wickedness after faith﴾: so do not do that, lest you deserve the name of wickedness. It is also said: its meaning is, "How evil is the name you give him when you say 'fasiq', after you know that he has believed."

﴿And whoever does not repent—it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, avoid much suspicion…﴾ [the verse]

The verse was revealed concerning two men among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who backbit two of their companions. This was because whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to fight or travel, he would attach a needy man to two wealthy men who would serve them, carry their provisions, and go ahead to the lodging to prepare for them what they needed of food and drink. In one of his journeys, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ attached Salman al-Farsi, may Allah be pleased with him, to two men. Salman went ahead, but his eyes overcame him (he fell asleep), and he prepared nothing for them. When they arrived, they said to him: "You have done nothing?" He said: "No." They said: "Why?" He said: "My eyes overcame me." They said: "Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him for food and condiment for us."

Salman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him for food. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Go to Usama ibn Zayd and say to him: 'If he has any surplus of food and condiment, let him give it to you.'" Usama was the treasurer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in charge of his baggage. [Salman] came to him, and he said: "I have nothing." Salman returned to the two and informed them of this. They said: "Usama had it, but he was stingy." They sent Salman to a group of the Companions, but he found nothing with them. When Salman returned, they said: "If we had sent him to the well of Sumayha, its water would have dried up." Then they went off, spying to see whether Usama had anything the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded for them.

When they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said to them: "What is it with me that I see the greenness of meat on your mouths?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, we have not tasted meat today." He said: "You have been eating the flesh of Salman and Usama."

Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, avoid much suspicion, for indeed some suspicion is sin; and do not spy…﴾

The majority read "tajassus" with a jim (tajassus), while Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Raja al-'Utaridi read "tahassus" with a ha'. Al-Akhfash said: Neither of them is far from the other.
