Ibn Manjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba told us, saying: al-Firyabi told us, saying: Qutayba ibn Sa'd told us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. And do not spy (wa-la tajassasu), nor seek out news (wa-la tahassasu), nor compete for worldly goods, nor envy one another, nor turn away from one another, but be, O servants of Allah, brothers."

Ibn Manjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Habash told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Zanjawayh informed us, saying: Salama told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Zurara ibn Mus'ab ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, that he stood guard one night with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab in Medina. While they were walking, a lamp appeared to them in a house, so they went toward it. When they drew near, they found a door ajar onto a people who had raised voices and noise. 'Umar took 'Abd al-Rahman by the hand and said: "Do you know whose house this is?" I said: "No." He said: "This is the house of Rabi'a ibn Umayya ibn Khalaf, and they are now drinking wine. So what do you think?" 'Abd al-Rahman said: "I think we have come to what Allah has forbidden, for He said: ﴿and do not spy﴾, and we have spied." So 'Umar turned away from them and left them.

And from him, from Ma'mar, who said: Ayyub informed me, from Abu Qilaba, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated that Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi drank wine in his house with his companions. 'Umar went until he entered upon him, and found no one there except one man. Abu Mihjan said: "O Commander of the Faithful, this is not lawful for you; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden you from spying." 'Umar said: "What is this man saying?" Zayd ibn Thabit and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Arqam said: "He is right, O Commander of the Faithful; this is spying." He said: So 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, went out and left him.

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab went out one night, accompanied by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, may Allah be pleased with both of them, patrolling. A fire appeared to them, so they came to the door and asked permission. The door was opened and they entered, and there was a man and a woman singing. In the man's hand was a cup. 'Umar said to the man: "And you are doing this, so-and-so?" He said: "And you are doing this, O Commander of the Faithful?" 'Umar said: "Who is this woman to you?" He said: "My wife." He said: "And what is in the cup?" He said: "Pure water." Then he said to the woman: "And what is it you are singing?" She said:

"I say:
The night has lengthened and its sides have darkened,
and sleeplessness has kept me awake, with no beloved to play with.
By Allah, were it not for fear of Allah and piety,
it would have shaken the sides of this couch from its place.
But my reason and my modesty suffice me,
and noble is my husband, that his mounts should be unreachable."

Then the man said: "We were not commanded with this, O Commander of the Faithful." 'Umar said: "Allah says: ﴿and do not spy﴾." 'Umar said: "You are right," and he left.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn 'Alawiyya told us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa told us, saying: al-Musayyib told us, from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: It was said to Ibn Mas'ud: "Would you like [to see] al-Walid ibn 'Uqba, whose beard is dripping with wine?" He said: "We have been forbidden from spying, so if something appears to us, we will take him to account for it."

It was said: "If what I say is true of him?" He said: "If it is in him, you have backbitten him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him."

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the people mentioned a man, saying: "He eats only what he is given, and he travels only with what he is provided; how weak he is!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have backbitten your brother." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, and is it backbiting to speak of what is in him?" He said: "It is enough for you to speak of your brother with what is in him."

Musa ibn Wardan narrated from Abu Hurayra that a man rose from beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they noticed in his rising a weakness. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how weak so-and-so is!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have eaten your brother's flesh and backbitten him."

﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ Qatada said: He means: just as you would hate it if you found a putrid corpse and were asked to eat from it, so hate the flesh of your brother while he is alive. ﴿You would hate it﴾: al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: its meaning is "then you have hated it." Abu Sa'id al-Khudri read "fa-kurrihtumuhu" with a shaddah, in the impersonal passive form.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Abu Salih 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abi 'Isma told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Isfahani told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym told us, from Kahmas, from Maymun ibn Siyah, who used to be preferred over al-Hasan—and it is said: he met those he had not met—who said: "While I was sleeping, I saw the corpse of a black man, and someone said to me: 'Eat.' I said: 'O servant of Allah, why should I eat?' He said: 'Because of your backbiting of So-and-so's slave.' I said: 'By Allah, I did not mention any good or evil about him.' He said: 'But you listened and approved.'" Maymun after that never backbit anyone, nor would he allow anyone to backbite in his presence.

It is related from one of the righteous that he said: "I was sitting in such-and-such a graveyard when a robust young man passed by me. I said: 'This one, and those like him, are a burden on people.' When that night came, I saw in a dream that a funeral bier was brought before me, with a dead person on it, and it was said to me: 'Eat from the flesh of this one.' He uncovered his face, and it was that young man. I said: 'I have not eaten the flesh of a lawful animal for years, so how could I eat this?' It was said: 'Then why did you backbite him?' I woke up grieving. I kept going back to that graveyard for a year, and then I saw the man. I stood up to ask his pardon, but he looked at me from afar and said: 'I have repented.' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Return to your place.'"

Ibn Manjawayh also informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, [who said] to Abu Hurayra: Ma'iz came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have committed adultery." He turned away from him until he confessed four times, and then he ordered that he be stoned. The Prophet ﷺ passed by two men who were talking about Ma'iz. One of them said: "This is the one who was concealed, but his soul did not leave him alone until he was stoned like a dog." He said: So he [the Prophet] remained silent about them until they passed with him by the carcass of a donkey with its leg stretched out. He ﷺ said to them: "Get down and eat from it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, may Allah forgive you! Is this carcass to be eaten?" He said: "What you have just eaten of your brother's flesh is more grievous for you. Indeed, he is now immersed in the rivers of Paradise."

Ibn Manjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba told us, saying: al-Firyabi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, saying: Abu al-Mughira told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj told us, saying: Safwan ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Rashid ibn Sa'd and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr told us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "When I was taken up on the Night Journey, I passed by a people who had claws of copper, scratching their faces and chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are the ones who eat people's flesh and attack their honour.'"

﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is Oft-Returning, Most Merciful.﴾

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Halwani told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Asbat told us, from Abu Raja al-Khurasani, from 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from al-Hariri, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Backbiting is worse than adultery." It was asked: "How so?" He said: "A man commits adultery, then repents, and Allah accepts his repentance; but the one who backbites is not forgiven until the one he backbit forgives him."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: al-Fadl told us, saying: Abu 'Isa Hamza ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Umar al-Bazzaz al-Baghdadi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Warraq told us, saying: Harun ibn Ma'ruf told us, saying: Dhamra told us, from Ibn Shudhi, who said: A man said to Ibn Sirin: "I have backbitten you, so make me lawful [of your forgiveness]." He said: "I dislike making lawful what Allah has made unlawful."

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: Abu al-Tayyib ibn Hafsawayh told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Jami' told us, saying: I read to Ahmad ibn Sa'id, saying: Sa'id told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Khalid al-Rab'i, who said: 'Isa ibn Maryam said to his companions: "Do you see, if one of you saw his Muslim brother with the wind having uncovered his garments?" They said: "Glory be to Allah! We would cover him." He said: "No, rather you would uncover what remains," as a parable he struck for them: they hear of a man's bad deed or good deed, and then they mention far more than that.

'Umar went until he entered upon him, and found no one there except one man. Abu Mihjan said: "O Commander of the Faithful, this is not lawful for you; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden you from spying." 'Umar said: "What is this man saying?" Zayd ibn Thabit and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Arqam said: "He is right, O Commander of the Faithful; this is spying." He said: So 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, went out and left him.

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab went out one night, accompanied by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, may Allah be pleased with both of them, patrolling. A fire appeared to them, so they came to the door and asked permission. The door was opened and they entered, and there was a man and a woman singing. In the man's hand was a cup. 'Umar said to the man: "And you are doing this, so-and-so?" He said: "And you are doing this, O Commander of the Faithful?" 'Umar said: "Who is this woman to you?" He said: "My wife." He said: "And what is in the cup?" He said: "Pure water." Then he said to the woman: "And what is it you are singing?" She said:

"I say:
The night has lengthened and its sides have darkened,
and sleeplessness has kept me awake, with no beloved to play with.
By Allah, were it not for fear of Allah and piety,
it would have shaken the sides of this couch from its place.
But my reason and my modesty suffice me,
and noble is my husband, that his mounts should be unreachable."

Then the man said: "We were not commanded with this, O Commander of the Faithful." 'Umar said: "Allah says: ﴿and do not spy﴾." 'Umar said: "You are right," and he left.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn 'Alawiyya told us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Isa told us, saying: al-Musayyib told us, from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: It was said to Ibn Mas'ud: "Would you like [to see] al-Walid ibn 'Uqba, whose beard is dripping with wine?" He said: "We have been forbidden from spying, so if something appears to us, we will take him to account for it."

﴿and do not backbite one another﴾

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub al-Muqri told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd Abu Bakr al-Sutawi told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ishkab told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami told us, saying: Jahdam ibn 'Abd Allah told us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about backbiting (ghiba), and he said: "It is that you mention your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "If what I say is true of him?" He said: "If it is in him, you have backbitten him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him."

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the people mentioned a man, saying: "He eats only what he is given, and he travels only with what he is provided; how weak he is!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have backbitten your brother." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, and is it backbiting to speak of what is in him?" He said: "It is enough for you to speak of your brother with what is in him."

Musa ibn Wardan narrated from Abu Hurayra that a man rose from beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they noticed in his rising a weakness. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how weak so-and-so is!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have eaten your brother's flesh and backbitten him."

﴿Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?﴾ Qatada said: He means: just as you would hate it if you found a putrid corpse and were asked to eat from it, so hate the flesh of your brother while he is alive. ﴿You would hate it﴾: al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: its meaning is "then you have hated it." Abu Sa'id al-Khudri read "fa-kurrihtumuhu" with a shaddah, in the impersonal passive form.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Umar ibn Nuh al-Bajali told us, saying: Abu Salih 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abi 'Isma told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Isfahani told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym told us, from Kahmas, from Maymun ibn Siyah, who used to be preferred over al-Hasan—and it is said: he met those he had not met—who said: "While I was sleeping, I saw the corpse of a black man, and someone said to me: 'Eat.' I said: 'O servant of Allah, why should I eat?' He said: 'Because of your backbiting of So-and-so's slave.' I said: 'By Allah, I did not mention any good or evil about him.' He said: 'But you listened and approved.'" Maymun after that never backbit anyone, nor would he allow anyone to backbite in his presence.

It is related from one of the righteous that he said: "I was sitting in such-and-such a graveyard when a robust young man passed by me. I said: 'This one, and those like him, are a burden on people.' When that night came, I saw in a dream that a funeral bier was brought before me, with a dead person on it, and it was said to me: 'Eat from the flesh of this one.' He uncovered his face, and it was that young man. I said: 'I have not eaten the flesh of a lawful animal for years, so how could I eat this?' It was said: 'Then why did you backbite him?' I woke up grieving. I kept going back to that graveyard for a year, and then I saw the man. I stood up to ask his pardon, but he looked at me from afar and said: 'I have repented.' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Return to your place.'"

Ibn Manjawayh also informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, [who said] to Abu Hurayra: Ma'iz came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have committed adultery." He turned away from him until he confessed four times, and then he ordered that he be stoned. The Prophet ﷺ passed by two men who were talking about Ma'iz. One of them said: "This is the one who was concealed, but his soul did not leave him alone until he was stoned like a dog." He said: So he [the Prophet] remained silent about them until they passed with him by the carcass of a donkey with its leg stretched out. He ﷺ said to them: "Get down and eat from it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, may Allah forgive you! Is this carcass to be eaten?" He said: "What you have just eaten of your brother's flesh is more grievous for you. Indeed, he is now immersed in the rivers of Paradise."

Ibn Manjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba told us, saying: al-Firyabi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, saying: Abu al-Mughira told us, saying: 'Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj told us, saying: Safwan ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Rashid ibn Sa'd and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr told us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "When I was taken up on the Night Journey, I passed by a people who had claws of copper, scratching their faces and chests. I said: 'Who are these, O Jibril?' He said: 'These are the ones who eat people's flesh and attack their honour.'"

﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is Oft-Returning, Most Merciful.﴾

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Halwani told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Asbat told us, from Abu Raja al-Khurasani, from 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from al-Hariri, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Backbiting is worse than adultery." It was asked: "How so?" He said: "A man commits adultery, then repents, and Allah accepts his repentance; but the one who backbites is not forgiven until the one he backbit forgives him."

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: al-Fadl told us, saying: Abu 'Isa Hamza ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Umar al-Bazzaz al-Baghdadi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Warraq told us, saying: Harun ibn Ma'ruf told us, saying: Dhamra told us, from Ibn Shudhi, who said: A man said to Ibn Sirin: "I have backbitten you, so make me lawful [of your forgiveness]." He said: "I dislike making lawful what Allah has made unlawful."

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: Abu al-Tayyib ibn Hafsawayh told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Jami' told us, saying: I read to Ahmad ibn Sa'id, saying: Sa'id told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Khalid al-Rab'i, who said: 'Isa ibn Maryam said to his companions: "Do you see, if one of you saw his Muslim brother with the wind having uncovered his garments?" They said: "Glory be to Allah! We would cover him." He said: "No, rather you would uncover what remains," as a parable he struck for them: they hear of a man's bad deed or good deed, and then they mention far more than that.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 49, verse 13–18:

﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes...﴾ [49:13]

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays and his saying to a man who did not make room for him: "Son of so-and-so's woman." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is it that mentions so-and-so's woman?" Thabit stood up and said: "I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Look at the faces of the people." So he looked at them, and he said: "What did you see, O Thabit?" He said: "I saw white, black, and red." He said: "You are not superior to them except in religion and piety." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse concerning Thabit, and concerning the man who was not given room: ﴿O you who believe, when it is said to you, "Make room in the assemblies," then make room...﴾ [58:11], and the rest of the verse.

Muqatil said: When the day of the conquest of Makkah came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Bilal to climb onto the roof of the Ka'bah and call the adhan. 'Attab ibn Asid ibn Abi al-'Is said: "Praise be to Allah who took my father before he saw this day." Al-Harith ibn Hisham said: "Did Muhammad not find anyone other than this black crow to be a muezzin?" Suhayl ibn 'Amr said: "If Allah wills something, He will change it." Abu Sufyan ibn Harb said: "I will not say anything, for I fear that the Lord of the heavens will inform of it."

So Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of what they had said. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them and asked them about what they had said, and they acknowledged it. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse and rebuked them for boasting of lineages, competing in wealth, and looking down upon the poor.

Yazid ibn Sakhrah said: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was passing through some of the markets of Madinah, and there was a black slave standing, being offered for sale, so whoever wanted him...

The slave had said: "Whoever buys me, on him is a condition." It was said: "What is it?" He said: "That he not prevent me from the five prayers behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So a man bought him on this condition, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see him at every obligatory prayer. Then one day he was missing, so he said to his companion: "Where is the slave?" He said: "He is feverish, O Messenger of Allah." He said to his companions: "Come, let us go and visit him." So they went with him and visited him. Then after some days he said to his companion: "How is the slave?" [80]

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the slave is in a bad way." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood, went in to him while he was departing, and he died in that state. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took charge of his washing, shrouding, and burial. Then the Muhajirun and the Ansar were greatly affected by this matter. The Muhajirun said: "We emigrated from our homes, our wealth, and our families, yet none of us saw in his life, illness, and death what this slave received from him." The Ansar said: "We sheltered him, supported him, and shared with him, yet he preferred an Abyssinian slave over us." So Allah, glorified is He, excused His Messenger (ﷺ) regarding what he had done concerning the slave, and showed them the superiority of piety, and Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes...﴾

These are the heads of tribes and their main bodies, such as Rabi'ah, Mudar, al-Aws, and al-Khazraj. Its singular is sha'b (with a fatha on the shin); they were so named because of their branching out and gathering, like the branching of tree limbs. The word sha'b is among the words with opposite meanings: it is said "sha'abtuhu" meaning I gathered it, and "sha'abtuhu" meaning I scattered it; and from this comes the saying for death: shu'ub.

﴿And tribes (qaba'il)﴾, which are below the peoples; its singular is qabilah, and they are Kindah from Rabi'ah and Tamim from Mudar. Below the tribes are the 'amā'ir, its singular 'imarah (with a fatha on the 'ayn), like Shaybān from Bakr and Darim from Tamim. Below the 'amā'ir are the buṭūn, its singular baṭn, such as the Banu Ghalib and Lu'ayy from Quraysh. Below the buṭūn are the afkhādh, its singular fakhdh, such as the Banu Hashim and Umayyah from the Banu Lu'ayy. Then the fasa'il and the 'asha'ir, whose singulars are fasilah and 'asheerah. It is also said: the shu'ub are from the non-Arabs, the qaba'il from the Arabs, and the asbat from the Banu Isra'il. Abu Razin and Abu Rawq said: the shu'ub are those who do not attach themselves to anyone, but are ascribed to cities, villages, and lands, while the qaba'il are the Arabs who are ascribed to their fathers.

﴿That you may know one another﴾: each of you recognizes the other through closeness or distance of lineage, not in order to boast. Al-A'mash read (liyata'arafu), and Ibn 'Abbas read (li-ya'rifu) without the alif.

﴿Indeed, the most noble of you﴾ with a fatha on the hamzah (inna akramakum) would be read so; but the common readers read (inna) with a kasra on the hamzah, as a new sentence, with the pause on the words "that you may know one another." ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.﴾ Qatadah said: In this verse, the noblest nobility is piety, and the basest baseness is immorality.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to be the most noble of people, let him fear Allah." [81]

He also said: "A man's nobility is his religion and his piety, his origin is his intellect, and his lineage is his character." [82]

Ibn 'Abbas said: The nobility of this world is wealth, and the nobility of the Hereafter is piety. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.﴾

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Ya'qub al-Maqdisi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Maqri narrated to us, saying: Ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated the Ka'bah on his she-camel al-Qaswa on the day of the conquest, touching the corner with his staff. He could not find a place to kneel in the mosque, until we brought him out to the bottom of the valley, and she knelt there. Then he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "To proceed, O people, Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Jahiliyyah and its boasting of ancestors" (and in some wordings: "and its glorifying of its forefathers"). "Mankind is only two types: a pious, righteous person who is noble before Allah, and a wicked, miserable person who is contemptible before Allah." Then he recited this verse: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes...﴾ and said: "I say this word of mine, and I ask Allah's forgiveness for myself and for you." [83]

And al-Husayn informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kabuli narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds, and you are only the children of Adam; ﴿the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾." [84]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hafsawayh narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Jami' al-Maqri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khadim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Talhah narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Allah, glorified is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: "I made lineage, and you made lineage; I made ﴿the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾, yet you say: 'So-and-so son of so-and-so.' Today I raise up My lineage and lower your lineages. Where are the righteous? Where are the righteous?" ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.﴾ [85]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqri narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the most noble of people?" He said: "The most righteous of them."

Ibn Habib recited to me, saying: Ibn Rumayh recited to us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Farhan recited to us:

"What does a servant do with the might of wealth?
Might, all of it, belongs to the one who fears Allah.
Whoever knows Allah, and the knowledge of Allah does not suffice him,
That one is the wretched."

﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed."﴾ [49:14]

It was revealed concerning a group of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, and then the Banu al-Hallaf ibn al-Harith ibn Sa'id, who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah in a year of drought, and they professed the testimony that there is no god but Allah, though they were not believers in secret. They corrupted the roads of Madinah with aggression and raised its prices. They would come and go before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "The Arabs have come to you with themselves on the backs of their mounts, and we have come to you with deeds, with dependents and offspring," placing him under obligation, "and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so and Banu so-and-so fought you," seeking charity and saying: "Give us." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse concerning them.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the Bedouins whom Allah mentioned in Surah al-Fath, who were the Bedouin tribes of Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and Ghifar, who used to say: "We believe in Allah," so that they would be safe for themselves and their property. When they were called to go forth to al-Hudaybiyah, they stayed behind. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Say: You have not believed, but say, "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts.﴾ That is, we have submitted and yielded out of fear of killing and captivity. Thus He informed that the reality of faith is affirmation by the heart, that its profession by the tongue and manifesting its precepts by the body is not faith without sincerity, whose place is the heart, and that Islam is other than faith.

Evidence for this is what

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juzqi informed us, reading it to him Muhammad ibn Zakariyya in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year three hundred and eighty-eight, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn al-Daghuli informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Layth al-Marwazi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Abdan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Amir informed me, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave to a group, while Sa'd was sitting among them. Sa'd said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left out a man among them and did not give him, though he was the one I liked best of them. So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with you regarding so-and-so? By Allah, I think he is a believer." The Messenger of Allah said: "Or a Muslim."

He was silent briefly, then what I knew of him overcame me, so I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with you regarding so-and-so? By Allah, I think he is a believer." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Or a Muslim."

He was silent briefly, then what I knew of him overcame me, so I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with you regarding so-and-so? By Allah, I think he is a believer." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Or a Muslim; for indeed I give to a man while another is dearer to me than him, out of fear that he will be thrown face-first into the Fire." [86]

So know that Islam is entering into peace (al-silm), which is obedience, submission, and following. It is said: "aslama al-rajul" when a man entered into al-silm, which is obedience, submission, and following. It is said: "aslama al-rajul" when he entered into al-silm, just as it is said: "ashta al-rajul" when he entered winter, "asaf" when he entered summer, "arba'" when he entered spring, and "aqhata" when he entered drought. Thus, among Islam is what is genuine obedience with the tongue, the bodies, and the heart, as in His saying, mighty and majestic, to Ibrahim: ﴿Submit; he said, "I have submitted."﴾ [2:131], and His saying: ﴿So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers. And We found there not a house except of the Muslims.﴾ [51:35–36]

And among it is what is submission by the tongue without the heart, and that is His saying: ﴿But say, "We have submitted,"﴾ and its clarification is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And faith has not yet entered your hearts. But if you obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ outwardly and inwardly, secretly and openly, ﴿He will not deprive you [of the reward] of your deeds at all﴾ — Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read (yalitkum) with an alif, and Abu Hatim preferred it, taking as evidence His saying: ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾ [52:21]; it is said "alata yalit alta," and the poet said:

"Convey to Banu Tha'l from me a message,
Carrying the effort of delivery, neither deprived nor false."

The others read (yalitkum) from "lata yalit lit," as Ru'bah said:

"And a night of dew I traveled,
and the night did not deprive me of its journey."

Both mean: He will not diminish you, nor wrong you, ﴿in your deeds at all.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Then He explained the reality of faith, saying: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and then have not doubted﴾, that is, they did not doubt the oneness of Allah, nor the prophethood of His prophets, nor what they believed in, but rather they were certain and sincere. [87]

﴿And they strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful﴾ in their faith, not those who embraced Islam out of fear of the sword and hope for gain.

When these two verses were revealed, the Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and swore by Allah that they were believers in secret and openly, but Allah knew otherwise about them. [88] So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Say: Do you inform Allah of your religion?﴾, meaning the religion you are upon.

﴿And Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things. They consider it a favor to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favor to me; rather, Allah has done a favor to you that He guided you to faith, if you are truthful.﴾ That is, by your Islam. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Talhah, and 'Isa read (ya'malun) with the "ya," while others read (ta'malun) with the "ta."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 49, verse 13–18:

﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes...﴾ [49:13]

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays and his saying to a man who did not make room for him: "Son of so-and-so's woman." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is it that mentions so-and-so's woman?" Thabit stood up and said: "I am, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Look at the faces of the people." So he looked at them, and he said: "What did you see, O Thabit?" He said: "I saw white, black, and red." He said: "You are not superior to them except in religion and piety." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse concerning Thabit, and concerning the man who was not given room: ﴿O you who believe, when it is said to you, "Make room in the assemblies," then make room...﴾ [58:11], and the rest of the verse.

Muqatil said: When the day of the conquest of Makkah came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Bilal to climb onto the roof of the Ka'bah and call the adhan. 'Attab ibn Asid ibn Abi al-'Is said: "Praise be to Allah who took my father before he saw this day." Al-Harith ibn Hisham said: "Did Muhammad not find anyone other than this black crow to be a muezzin?" Suhayl ibn 'Amr said: "If Allah wills something, He will change it." Abu Sufyan ibn Harb said: "I will not say anything, for I fear that the Lord of the heavens will inform of it."

So Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of what they had said. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them and asked them about what they had said, and they acknowledged it. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse and rebuked them for boasting of lineages, competing in wealth, and looking down upon the poor.

Yazid ibn Sakhrah said: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was passing through some of the markets of Madinah, and there was a black slave standing, being offered for sale, so whoever wanted him...

The slave had said: "Whoever buys me, on him is a condition." It was said: "What is it?" He said: "That he not prevent me from the five prayers behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So a man bought him on this condition, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see him at every obligatory prayer. Then one day he was missing, so he said to his companion: "Where is the slave?" He said: "He is feverish, O Messenger of Allah." He said to his companions: "Come, let us go and visit him." So they went with him and visited him. Then after some days he said to his companion: "How is the slave?" [80]

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the slave is in a bad way." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood, went in to him while he was departing, and he died in that state. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took charge of his washing, shrouding, and burial. Then the Muhajirun and the Ansar were greatly affected by this matter. The Muhajirun said: "We emigrated from our homes, our wealth, and our families, yet none of us saw in his life, illness, and death what this slave received from him." The Ansar said: "We sheltered him, supported him, and shared with him, yet he preferred an Abyssinian slave over us." So Allah, glorified is He, excused His Messenger (ﷺ) regarding what he had done concerning the slave, and showed them the superiority of piety, and Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes...﴾

These are the heads of tribes and their main bodies, such as Rabi'ah, Mudar, al-Aws, and al-Khazraj. Its singular is sha'b (with a fatha on the shin); they were so named because of their branching out and gathering, like the branching of tree limbs. The word sha'b is among the words with opposite meanings: it is said "sha'abtuhu" meaning I gathered it, and "sha'abtuhu" meaning I scattered it; and from this comes the saying for death: shu'ub.

﴿And tribes (qaba'il)﴾, which are below the peoples; its singular is qabilah, and they are Kindah from Rabi'ah and Tamim from Mudar. Below the tribes are the 'amā'ir, its singular 'imarah (with a fatha on the 'ayn), like Shaybān from Bakr and Darim from Tamim. Below the 'amā'ir are the buṭūn, its singular baṭn, such as the Banu Ghalib and Lu'ayy from Quraysh. Below the buṭūn are the afkhādh, its singular fakhdh, such as the Banu Hashim and Umayyah from the Banu Lu'ayy. Then the fasa'il and the 'asha'ir, whose singulars are fasilah and 'asheerah. It is also said: the shu'ub are from the non-Arabs, the qaba'il from the Arabs, and the asbat from the Banu Isra'il. Abu Razin and Abu Rawq said: the shu'ub are those who do not attach themselves to anyone, but are ascribed to cities, villages, and lands, while the qaba'il are the Arabs who are ascribed to their fathers.

﴿That you may know one another﴾: each of you recognizes the other through closeness or distance of lineage, not in order to boast. Al-A'mash read (liyata'arafu), and Ibn 'Abbas read (li-ya'rifu) without the alif.

﴿Indeed, the most noble of you﴾ with a fatha on the hamzah (inna akramakum) would be read so; but the common readers read (inna) with a kasra on the hamzah, as a new sentence, with the pause on the words "that you may know one another." ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.﴾ Qatadah said: In this verse, the noblest nobility is piety, and the basest baseness is immorality.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to be the most noble of people, let him fear Allah." [81]

He also said: "A man's nobility is his religion and his piety, his origin is his intellect, and his lineage is his character." [82]

Ibn 'Abbas said: The nobility of this world is wealth, and the nobility of the Hereafter is piety. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.﴾

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Ya'qub al-Maqdisi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Maqri narrated to us, saying: Ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulated the Ka'bah on his she-camel al-Qaswa on the day of the conquest, touching the corner with his staff. He could not find a place to kneel in the mosque, until we brought him out to the bottom of the valley, and she knelt there. Then he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "To proceed, O people, Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Jahiliyyah and its boasting of ancestors" (and in some wordings: "and its glorifying of its forefathers"). "Mankind is only two types: a pious, righteous person who is noble before Allah, and a wicked, miserable person who is contemptible before Allah." Then he recited this verse: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes...﴾ and said: "I say this word of mine, and I ask Allah's forgiveness for myself and for you." [83]

And al-Husayn informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kabuli narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds, and you are only the children of Adam; ﴿the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾." [84]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hafsawayh narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Jami' al-Maqri narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khadim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Talhah narrated to us, from 'Ata', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Allah, glorified is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: "I made lineage, and you made lineage; I made ﴿the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾, yet you say: 'So-and-so son of so-and-so.' Today I raise up My lineage and lower your lineages. Where are the righteous? Where are the righteous?" ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.﴾ [85]

Ibn Manjawayh informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqri narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the most noble of people?" He said: "The most righteous of them."

Ibn Habib recited to me, saying: Ibn Rumayh recited to us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Farhan recited to us:

"What does a servant do with the might of wealth?
Might, all of it, belongs to the one who fears Allah.
Whoever knows Allah, and the knowledge of Allah does not suffice him,
That one is the wretched."

﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed."﴾ [49:14]

It was revealed concerning a group of the Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, and then the Banu al-Hallaf ibn al-Harith ibn Sa'id, who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madinah in a year of drought, and they professed the testimony that there is no god but Allah, though they were not believers in secret. They corrupted the roads of Madinah with aggression and raised its prices. They would come and go before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "The Arabs have come to you with themselves on the backs of their mounts, and we have come to you with deeds, with dependents and offspring," placing him under obligation, "and we did not fight you as Banu so-and-so and Banu so-and-so fought you," seeking charity and saying: "Give us." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse concerning them.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning the Bedouins whom Allah mentioned in Surah al-Fath, who were the Bedouin tribes of Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and Ghifar, who used to say: "We believe in Allah," so that they would be safe for themselves and their property. When they were called to go forth to al-Hudaybiyah, they stayed behind. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Say: You have not believed, but say, "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts.﴾ That is, we have submitted and yielded out of fear of killing and captivity. Thus He informed that the reality of faith is affirmation by the heart, that its profession by the tongue and manifesting its precepts by the body is not faith without sincerity, whose place is the heart, and that Islam is other than faith.
